question.text: Under Solon, all Athenian citizens were allowed to participate in the ekklesia assembly that met in a building southwest of this elevated part of the city, which is home to the Parthenon.
question.clue: This site of the Propylaea also featured six women taking the place of columns on its Caryatid Porch.

swap.text: This son of Philip II launched the Hellenistic era by conquering Persia under Darius III after battles such as Issus and Gaugamela.
swap.answerHtml: Alexander the Great [accept Alexander III or Alexander of Macedonia]
swap.clue: This leader declined to join the voyage of his admiral Nearchus because he was too busy executing people like Polymachus, who had desecrated the tomb of Cyrus.

question.leadin: A navigational aid on the coast of Galicia in northwest Spain, dating from the first century CE, is namedafter this mythical man because it marks the western limit of his travels.
question.text: Name this strongman from Roman myth who wore the skin of the Nemean Lion.
question.answerHtml: Hercules (acceptTower of Hercules; acceptTorre deHércules; do not accept or prompt on"Heracles")

swap.leadin: Answer the following about historians of the ancient world.
swap.text: Despite telling tales of giant ants and massive armies, this Greek is known as the "Father of Histories" for his work the Histories, which details the Persian Wars in addition to providing interesting if not accurate ethnographies of various classical peoples.
swap.clue: This author likely confused marmots for giant gold-digging ants in India.

question.leadin: The first half of this war ended with the signing of the Peace of Nicias.
question.text: Name this 5th century BCE war, fought for almost thirty years, between Athens and Sparta.
question.clue: The traitor Alcibiades led the ill-fated Sicilian Expedition for one side in this war that ultimately lost at the 405 BC Battle of Aegospotami.

swap.leadin: Pliny the Elder claimed that being touched by this ruler's right big toe would cure inflammation of the spleen.
swap.text: Name this ruler who apocryphally said "another such victory... and we are undone" after winning the Battle of Asculum, giving rise to a term for an overly costly victory.
swap.clue: Lysimachus ended this man's short first reign as King of Macedon, but this man later regained that title shortly before he died in Argos.

question.text: This Macedonian king was the wife of Olympias and the father of Alexander. He won the Battle of Chaeronea and was assassinated by Pausanias.
question.clue: Fireships were used against a military force launched by this monarch under the Duke of Medina-Sidonia prior to the Battle of Gravelines.

swap.leadin: Part of the ruins of this civilization were excavated by Sir Arthur Evans.
swap.text: Name this ancestor of the Mycenean civilization, which may have had some of its cities destroyed by the eruption of Thera.
swap.clue: One of this civilization's palaces is where the mysterious Phaistos disc was found.

question.leadin: A failed rebellion on this island in 1770 was led by a shipbuilder named Daskalogiannis.
question.text: Identify this island where the Venetians surrendered at Candia after a lengthy siege in 1669. The Phaistos Disc was found on this island, which in ancient times was home to a bull-jumping cult.
question.clue: Arthur Evans identified a culture on this island that may have been wiped out by the Thera eruption, whose inhabitants used the Linear A script.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about life before and after Alexander the Great.
swap.text: With a name from the Greek word for "succesors," these men took over Alexander's empire after his death. They included Ptolemy, Seleucus, and Antigonus.
swap.clue: Conflict between these people began when their former leader granted his kingdom "to the strongest."

question.leadin: This symbolic script used to write Mycenaean Greek was found on tablets on Crete in the early 20th century.
question.text: What is this written script which was deciphered by Michael Ventris?
question.clue: This system consists of ninety syllabic signs, all of which correspond to open syllables.

swap.text: Spartan slaves were known by this name. These people could become semi-free mothakes by undergoing the agoge education system.
swap.clue: These people were the target of an annual declaration of war by elected Ephors, who would pardon their killers from miasma.

question.leadin: This man legendarily promulgated an oral constitution that established the Gerousia, a council of 28 elders.
question.text: Name this lawgiver whose Rhetra also included a dual monarchy for Sparta.
question.clue: This legendary lawgiver who established the Great Rhetra constitution, outlined the function of the five ephors, and called for a council of twenty-eight men known as the gerousia to wield equal power to the two royal houses.

swap.text: This Spartan general, who was victorious at the battle of Aegospotami, took over Athens and set up the Thirty Tyrants.
swap.clue: This beneficiary of Cyrus the Younger's patronage resumed his most famous office after his replacement Callicratidas lost the battle of Arginusae.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Serpent Column.
question.text: According to Herodotus, the Serpent Column was created after this Greek victory, which took place on the same day as the Battle of Mycale. This 479 BC loss for Mardonius largely ended the wars between Greece and Persia.
question.clue: Despite the long preliminaries to this battle, the Eleans and Mantineans still managed to arrive after it ended.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the influence of classical writers on American political rhetoric.
swap.text: This Roman historian's praise of the Senate as an aristocratic check on the rights of the people heavily inspired John Adams' "A Defense of the Constitutions." This formulator of the concept of anacyclosis is also known for creating a grid display of letters of the alphabet often used in telegraphy and codes.
swap.clue: After that, he became a tutor to the sons of the general Lucius Aemilius Paulus, including Scipio Africanus, whom he followed to witness the destruction of Carthage.

question.text: The Panhellenic colony of Thurii (thoo-ree-"eye") was established at the direction of Pericles in this larger region. This term refers to colonies like Croton and Sybaris that first brought Greek culture to southern Italy and Sicily.
question.clue: Tarquin the Proud died in exile in a city in this region.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Thrasybulus, the arch-democrat who repeatedly thwarted Athenian oligarchic regimes such as the short-lived 400 and the more durable and brutal Thirty Tyrants.
swap.text: Thrasybulus prevented the 400's takeover of this island, led in a namesake war against Athens by the philosopher Melissus. Polycrates had The Tunnel of Eupalinos, an advanced underground aqueduct, built on it.
swap.clue: Herodotus claims that the pharaoh Ahmose broke off Egypt's alliance with this city-state after its tyrant discovered his lost ring in the belly of a fish.

question.leadin: Identify the following about the history of Corinth.
question.text: After the dissolution of the League of Corinth, the city became a part of this confederation led by Aratus of Sicyon, formed to protect the namesake region from Cleomenes III of Sparta.
question.clue: A brief war named for this power took place after the Romans defeated Andriscus in the Fourth Macedonian War.

swap.leadin: The terms on which Sicily became a Roman province obliged Rome to abide by the Law of Hiero and tax tenant farmers no more than 1/10th the value of their output.
swap.text: Hiero was a tyrant of this city, which had been an ally of Rome's in the first Punic War. This city joined the Carthaginians in the second war and the city was sacked, though not before the quasi-mythical burning of Roman ships with an enormous death ray.
swap.clue: The Spartan general Gyllipus defended this city from Athenians under Nicias during an expedition in the Peloponnesian War, and it was originally a Corinthian colony.
